subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Really appreciate the candid product context you shared (primary use: conversational support + dynamic recommendations, peak concurrency ~350 reqs/min with median prompt ~120 tokens). Per our conversation I ran a focused set of evals and put together a short recommended shortlist that balances cost, latency, and quality for your workload. See the attached summary and prompt set for details.

Top-line recommended shortlist (ordered by recommended default):

1) Redwood-2-13B-quant (recommended default)
   - Rationale: Best mid-tier tradeoff — near-human quality on your support prompts after a small instruction-tuning pass, 3–5x lower inference cost vs 70B-class models when running quantized on our Dedicated pools.
   - Latency: median token latency ~8–12 ms on A100-equivalent; end-to-end generation (avg 150 tokens) ~220–280 ms under expected concurrency with our batching config.
   - Cost: ~0.6x of a 70B model (per-turn token cost) when using q4_0 quant profile + caching.
   - Risks: Slightly lower long-context coherence on multi-step reasoning vs 70B; we recommend the included prompt-set augmentation to mitigate.

2) Llama-3-70B (high-quality fallback)
   - Rationale: Highest quality for complex multi-step dialogue and coding-style answers; useful as a fallback model for escalation flows where precision matters.
   - Latency: median token latency ~25–35 ms on A100-equivalent; 150-token turn typically 700–900 ms without aggressive batching.
   - Cost: ~3–4x Redwood-2-13B-quant per-token.
   - Risks: Higher cost/latency; we recommend using routing policies so only a small % of traffic hits this model (canary/2–5% escalation).

3) Open-Adapter-15B (cost-optimized alternative)
   - Rationale: Good cost/quality balance for high-throughput notification/templating flows where extreme accuracy is not required.
   - Latency: similar to 13B when quantized (~10–18 ms median token latency).
   - Cost: slightly lower than Redwood-2-13B-quant on some configs but requires additional prompt engineering.

Attachments included: acme_benchmark_summary.pdf (benchmarks & evals), prompt_set_v1.csv (seed prompts & expected outputs), redwood_model_cost_table.xlsx (detailed per-model cost math).

Next steps I propose:
- You review the attached prompt_set_v1 and flag any high-risk prompts (security/privacy-sensitive items).
- We run a 3-day eval with your top 200 production prompts (we can host in a dedicated evaluation project).
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review results and agree routing (default model + escalation %).

If useful, Vivek can jump in with a short note on quant latency and token pricing — Rafael and Vivek are cc'd.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0104

Thanks Marissa — this is really helpful. Quick clarifying Qs:
1) Can you call out expected p95 latency for Redwood-2-13B-quant at our concurrency (350 reqs/min)?
2) For regulatory reasons we need to understand PII handling in evals: can ACME-only evals run in an isolated Dedicated pool and can logs be disabled/filtered for those runs?

If you can answer those two we can get the security team looped and approve the 3-day eval.

—Alex
Head of Product, ACME Corp
alex.j@acme.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-demo: recommended model shortlist & next steps

Hi Alex —

Short answers: yes to isolated runs, and yes to filtered logs. A few technical details below: 

- Isolation & logs: We can run the 3-day evaluation inside a Dedicated evaluation pool provisioned for ACME-only traffic. For that run we can apply log redaction at ingestion (PII regex filters) and disable token-level audit logging if required; we will persist only aggregated metrics and anonymized examples unless you request storage of raw transcriptions.

- Latency at 350 reqs/min: For Redwood-2-13B-quant on a standard Dedicated A100 node with our recommended batching (dynamic batching + caching TTL=30s), observed p95 token latency in our ACME-like sims is ~22–28 ms; end-to-end p95 for a 150-token generation is ~650–820 ms under the load profile you described. The attached cost table has simulation knobs we used.

- Quality regression concern: We noticed in a couple of the eval prompts that Llama-3-70B outperforms the 13B on long multi-step reasoning. If you have a small set of high-stakes prompts, please flag them and we'll run an expanded diff-eval and provide failure-mode examples so you can decide threshold-based routing (e.g., route to 70B when prompt contains escalation keywords or when a quality confidence metric is below X).

Links & tooling:
- Evaluation harness (demo project): https://docs.redwood.ai/benchmarks/acme-2026-summary
- Prompt set folder (seed prompts & labels): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExamplePromptSet

I'll coordinate with Ops to provision an isolated evaluation cluster once ACME security signs off.

Cheers,
Rafael
Principal Applied ML, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai

---
Note: simulation numbers assume our q4_0 quant profile; real-world p95 can vary with network/cold-cache conditions.
